sentences.text: Wpcrl/254/2021 on 12 November, 2024

Author: Manoj Kumar Tiwari
Bench: Manoj Kumar Tiwari
Office Notes, reports, orders Sl. or proceedings Date Court'S Or Judges'S Order
S No or directions and Registrar's order with Signatures Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J. None for the petitioner.
Mr. Deepak Bhardwaj, Brief Holder, for the State.

(2) Petitioner has sought quashing of FIR No. 0043 of 2021 lodged against him in PS Haldwani,
District Nainital for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468 IPC.

Coordinate Bench of this Court had passed an interim order in favour of petitioner that no coercive action shall be taken against him pursuant to the said FIR provided he cooperates with the investigating agency.

(3)
Learned State Counsel submits that upon investigation, chargesheet has been filed against petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 120B IPC before the trial court by the investigating agency.
He thus submits that writ petition has become infructuous and petitioner can challenge the chargesheet in proceedings under Section 482 CrPC (now, Section 528 of BNSS), if so advised.
(4) Writ petition does not become infructuous merely because chargesheet is filed.
I have gone through the impugned FIR, which is on record as Annexure-1 to the writ petition.
Specific allegations have been made against the petitioner.
It is not the case that necessary ingredients of the alleged offences are not made out.
Whether the allegations are correct or incorrect cannot be gone into by this Court in a writ petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution.
It is a matter of trial.
Although petitioner contends that he has been falsely implicated in this case, the said contention cannot be considered by this Court at this stage.

(5) In an authoritative judicial pronouncement rendered in the case of M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra & others, reported in AIR 2021 SC 1918, Hon'ble Supreme has set out parameters for quashing the FIR.

entities.text: M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra & others, reported in AIR 2021 SC 1918
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: None of those parameters is met for quashing the impugned FIR.
Thus there is no scope for interference.
(6) Writ petition thus fails and is dismissed.

(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J.) 12.11.2024 Pr WPCRL/254/2021 on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39506696/
